findings.title: Filial status meets unshared rule
findings.claim: The offspring attribution can also carry a possible status or succession implication that the pericope's exclusive lordship, absent guardianship, and unshared judgment close off.
findings.mechanism: The focus offspring carrier meets 18:14's exclusive Lordship, 18:17 and 18:26's unavailable alternative guardian, and 18:26's rejection of any partner in judgment; the relation shifts from biological lineage alone toward possible shared status.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the surrounding negations address more than family vocabulary: they also close routes to co-status, succession, guardianship, or shared rule.
findings.containment: The status-and-succession implication is an attributed medium-strength inference. The word may be rejected solely as lineage, and the context does not force one motive. The biological offspring reading remains live.

epistemic.reason: The exact HFT coordinates supply the focus return and all contextual roles, but the reader identity is legacy_unbound and the status implication is explicitly qualified in the trace.
